transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope it's okay that I'm here. I guess I came in because... well, I've been trying to clean up my image and my routine lately for this arts board stuff I do. And I thought it would be a really positive thing, but I've actually been feeling a bit more tense and... maybe a little down? Just more than I expected to be. 

I mean, I'm still doing the basics, I promise I'm keeping up with the main stuff! But I just keep dropping these little things I usually really care about, like my fair planning notes or my design drafts. And then I feel so guilty about it that I end up canceling plans with people instead of just catching up on the work. 

I'm sorry, I know it probably sounds a bit silly, and I'm sure you see people with much bigger problems, but... does that make sense for why I'd be here?
Have you been feeling anxious lately?

Um... anxious? I don't think so. I mean, definitely not anything severe! I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, I promise I'm holding it together for the most part. 

It's really just... that tense feeling I mentioned before. Like, just wanting to make sure I'm doing a good job with the board and worrying a little about letting people down. But I wouldn't really call it anxiety. Unless... do you think that counts as being anxious? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer and not, you know, exaggerating things.
Have you been feeling sad most of the day?

Oh, no, definitely not most of the day! Um, I know I mentioned feeling a little down earlier, but I really want to make sure I'm being clear that it's just... little moments here and there. I try really hard to stay positive, and I'm usually a pretty upbeat person! 

It's mostly just when I think about falling behind on my fair notes or when I have to cancel on someone. But I wouldn't say it lasts all day at all. I hope it's okay that I'm not feeling *that* bad... I really don't want you to think I'm taking up your time for no reason if I'm not, you know, sad all the time. Is it normal to just have it be quick little moments like that?
Have you been enjoying things you usually like to do?

Um, yeah, I think so! I mean, I still really enjoy the arts board stuff when I'm actually doing it. And I still like my hobbies... I just haven't been doing them quite as much lately because of all the pressure I've been putting on myself. 

But when I do get around to them, I definitely still like them! I'm not, like, sitting around feeling empty or anything. I really try to appreciate the good things. Do you think it's okay that I'm just a little distracted from them right now, rather than not enjoying them at all?
Are there things that you used to enjoy, but now you don't find pleasure in them at all?

No, no, nothing like that! I promise I haven't lost interest in everything. I'm really trying to keep up with the things I love. 

I mean, maybe I'm just a little too focused on making sure the board stuff is perfect right now, so I don't have as much time for other things. But if I had the time, I'd still love them just as much! I really don't want to sound like I'm giving up on things or, you know, being ungrateful for the fun stuff in my life. It's just a time-management thing, really. That makes sense, right? Like, it's normal to just be a little too busy sometimes?
Have you lost any weight recently?

Oh, no, I haven't! My weight has been pretty much exactly the same. I've been really careful to make sure I'm still eating regularly, even when I get a little overwhelmed with all my notes and things. 

I know it's important to take care of myself, so I definitely haven't been skipping meals or anything like that. My clothes all still fit perfectly fine. That's a good sign, right? That I'm keeping my appetite up and staying healthy?
Do you often feel guilty about things that aren't your fault?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean... I try really hard to keep a good perspective on things like that. If something goes wrong and it's genuinely not my fault, I don't sit around beating myself up over it. 

I really try to be rational and just focus on what I can actually control, you know? I know it's not helpful or productive to take on blame for things I didn't do, so I do my best to just let those things go and move forward. That's a pretty healthy way to look at it, don't you think? Just trying to be fair to myself?
Has something specific and stressful happened to you recently?

Well, um... I guess that's sort of why I decided to come in. I mean, it's not like a huge, terrible tragedy or anything! Just... I've been really trying to clean up my image and my whole routine for this arts board I'm on. I want to make a good impression, you know? 

But since I started trying to do all that, I've just been feeling a lot more tense and... maybe a little more down than I expected to. I'm still doing all the basic, important stuff, I promise! But I keep sort of... dropping the ball on little things I normally care a lot about, like my notes for the fair planning or my design drafts. 

And then... well, then I feel really bad about it, and instead of just catching up like a normal person, I end up canceling plans with people. Which I know isn't great. But I'm really trying to get back on track! It's just a little bit of an adjustment period, right? Like, it's normal to get a little stressed when you're trying to improve yourself?
Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or activities because of your concerns about not doing them perfectly?

Oh, no, I don't think so. It's really not about things needing to be perfect! I mean, I know I mentioned canceling some social plans earlier, but that's mostly just because I feel bad about falling behind on my work, not because I'm afraid of doing things imperfectly. 

I always try my best to just... show up and do what I need to do, especially for the board, even if my work isn't absolutely flawless. I know nobody's perfect, and I definitely wouldn't want to let people down by just avoiding a task altogether just because I'm nervous about it. I think it's much better to just give it your best effort rather than hide away from it. That's a good mindset to have, right? Just doing your best and being okay with it?
Have you experienced any traumatic events in your life?

Oh, goodness, no. No, definitely not. I mean... I've been really lucky in that regard. I haven't been through anything terrible like that. 

I've had a pretty, um, normal, safe life, I guess you could say. I really try to just focus on the good things and be grateful for what I have, you know? I think it's always better to look at the bright side and appreciate the positive things instead of looking for the bad. That's a good way to be, right? Just trying to stay positive?
Are there things you used to find pleasurable, but now you only do out of obligation?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I still really enjoy the things I've always liked! Like my design work and helping out with the arts community... I still find a lot of joy in all of that. I promise I'm not just going through the motions or doing it just because I have to. 

I guess sometimes I feel a little tired before I start a project, just because I've been trying so hard to get everything right, but once I'm actually doing it, I still have fun. I think it's really important to keep finding the good in your hobbies, even if you're going through a little bit of a stressful patch, you know? It's good to keep enjoying life as much as you can... wouldn't you agree?
Do you often feel like you're not good enough?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, sure, everyone has moments where they doubt themselves a little bit, right? But I don't walk around feeling like I'm not good enough in general. 

I know I've been a little stressed lately with everything going on, but I still believe in myself and my abilities. I really try to focus on my strengths and the things I do well, rather than beating myself up over every little thing. I think it's so important to be kind to yourself, especially when things are a little overwhelming. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it? Just trying to stay confident and not be too hard on yourself?
Have you been having trouble sleeping due to worries or concerns?

Oh, sleep? No, I've been sleeping fine, really. I mean, maybe it takes me a tiny bit longer to drift off sometimes if I have a lot on my mind, but that's normal, right? Everyone has nights where they think about their day a little bit before they fall asleep. 

I definitely wouldn't say I'm having trouble sleeping or lying awake worrying all night. I always try to do a little deep breathing or think of happy things if my mind is racing, and that usually does the trick. It's so important to get a good night's rest so you can tackle the next day with a positive attitude. That's a healthy way to look at it, don't you think? Just making sure you get enough rest to keep going?
Do you feel overwhelmed by your emotions most of the time?

Oh, overwhelmed? No, no, I wouldn't say most of the time. I mean, sure, I've had a few moments lately where I felt a little... flustered, maybe? Just with the changes happening and trying to figure things out. But I definitely don't feel overwhelmed by my emotions all the time. 

I really try my best to keep a positive outlook and just take things one step at a time. If I start feeling a little stressed, I just remind myself that everything will work out and try to focus on the good things. It's better to just keep a smile on and push through, right? You have to stay strong and not let things get to you too much... that's the best way to handle it, isn't it?
Do you feel like you're struggling to cope with your emotions lately?

Struggling? Oh, no, I wouldn't use that word. I mean, I'm definitely still managing everything just fine. 

I guess there are moments where I feel a tiny bit sad or... you know, just a little off, but I always bounce back pretty quickly. I just try to keep myself busy and focus on the positives. I think everyone gets a little teary sometimes when things are changing, right? It's just a normal way to let it out so you can keep moving forward. As long as I'm still getting up and trying my best every day, that means I'm coping okay, right? What do you think?
Do you often feel worthless?

Worthless? Oh, gosh, no. That's a really strong word. I definitely don't feel worthless. 

I mean, maybe sometimes I feel a little... unproductive? Just because I'm not working right now since I finished my Associate's, and I'm still trying to figure out my next steps. So there are days where I think, "Oh, I should be doing more." But I know I have value and I'm a good person. I just try to remind myself that this is a transition period and I'll find my way soon. It's totally normal to feel a little lost when you're between things, right? I'm just trying to stay positive and keep looking for opportunities. That's the right attitude to have, don't you think?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, I guess... maybe about two months? It really hasn't been that long. 

It started right around the time I decided to, you know, overhaul my daily routine and how I present myself. I just wanted to make some positive changes and put my best foot forward while I'm figuring things out. So, naturally, adjusting to all those new habits has just made me feel a little bit tired or off some days. But two months isn't really that long to be adjusting to a new schedule, is it? I feel like it takes anyone a little time to get used to a big routine change, right?
Have you noticed any change in your weight over the past two months?

Weight? Oh, um, no, not really. I mean, my clothes still fit exactly the same, so I think I've stayed pretty steady. 

I try to make sure I'm eating well and taking care of myself, especially with all the new routine changes. I might skip a snack here or there if I'm busy, or maybe treat myself to something sweet if I'm feeling a little stressed, but nothing major at all. I'm definitely staying healthy. That's really important when you're going through a transition, isn't it? Just keeping everything balanced?
Was there a specific event or change that triggered your decision to overhaul your daily routine and image?

Well, um, it wasn't really a single bad event or anything like that. It was actually a really positive opportunity! I got involved with this local arts board, which is just so exciting. But, you know, it's a very... polished group of people. 

So I just realized I needed a bit of an image reset to really fit in and be taken seriously. That's why I started changing up my clothes, my daily routines, and even, um, who I was spending most of my time with. I just wanted to make sure I was presenting myself the right way for this new role. It was a few weeks after I started making all those changes for the arts board that I started feeling a little... off. But it's completely normal to want to put your best foot forward when you join a new group, right? It's just a lot to adjust to all at once, wouldn't you agree?
Do you find yourself avoiding social interactions because you feel like you're not living up to your own expectations?

Well, um... maybe a little bit? I mean, I wouldn't say I'm *avoiding* people, exactly. It's more just... 

Since I started trying to, you know, clean up my image and my routine for all the arts board stuff, I've just been a little more tense and... maybe a tiny bit more down than I expected to be. I'm still doing all the basic, important things, of course! But I guess I've been dropping some of the little things I usually really care about. Like, I haven't been keeping up with my fair planning notes or my design drafts like I should. 

And then... well, I just feel a little guilty about it. So sometimes, instead of going out, I might cancel a plan here or there, just so I can try to catch up on those things. But that's a pretty normal reaction to feeling a little behind, right? It's responsible to stay in and work on things instead of going out when you have a lot on your plate, don't you think?
